## Solution

We evaluate $I=\displaystyle\int_{-\infty}^{\infty}\arcsin\!\left(\frac{1}{\cosh x}\right)dx$.

**Symmetry.** The integrand is even, so
$$I=2\int_{0}^{\infty}\arcsin(\operatorname{sech}x)\,dx.$$

**Substitution.** Set $t=\operatorname{sech}x$. Then $t:1\to 0$ as $x:0\to\infty$, and
$$dt=-\operatorname{sech}x\,\tanh x\,dx=-t\sqrt{1-t^{2}}\,dx,\qquad\text{so}\quad dx=\frac{-dt}{t\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}.$$
Hence
$$I=2\int_{0}^{1}\frac{\arcsin t}{t\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}\,dt.$$

**Integration by parts.** Take
$$u=\arcsin t,\quad du=\frac{dt}{\sqrt{1-t^{2}}};\qquad dv=\frac{dt}{t\sqrt{1-t^{2}}},\quad v=\ln\!\frac{t}{1+\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}.$$
(The antiderivative follows from $t=\sin\theta$: $\int\frac{dt}{t\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}=\int\csc\theta\,d\theta=\ln\tan\frac{\theta}{2}=\ln\frac{t}{1+\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}+C$.)

Boundary terms: at $t=1$, $u=\pi/2$, $v=\ln 1=0$; at $t\to0^{+}$, $u\sim t$, $v\sim\ln(t/2)$, so $uv\to0$. Thus
$$I=-2\int_{0}^{1}\ln\!\frac{t}{1+\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}\cdot\frac{dt}{\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}=2\int_{0}^{1}\frac{-\ln t}{\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}\,dt+2\int_{0}^{1}\frac{\ln(1+\sqrt{1-t^{2}})}{\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}\,dt.$$

**First integral.** With $t=\sin\theta$,
$$\int_{0}^{1}\frac{-\ln t}{\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}\,dt=\int_{0}^{\pi/2}(-\ln\sin\theta)\,d\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}\ln 2.$$
So the first part contributes $\pi\ln 2$.

**Second integral.** Again $t=\sin\theta$:
$$J:=\int_{0}^{1}\frac{\ln(1+\sqrt{1-t^{2}})}{\sqrt{1-t^{2}}}\,dt=\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\ln(1+\cos\theta)\,d\theta.$$
Using $1+\cos\theta=2\cos^{2}\!\frac{\theta}{2}$,
$$J=\frac{\pi}{2}\ln 2+2\int_{0}^{\pi/2}\ln\cos\frac{\theta}{2}\,d\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}\ln 2+4\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\ln\cos\phi\,d\phi.$$

**Catalan's constant.** Let $G=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n}}{(2n+1)^{2}}=-\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\ln\tan\phi\,d\phi$ be Catalan's constant. The standard identities
$$\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\ln\cos\phi\,d\phi+\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\ln\sin\phi\,d\phi=-\frac{\pi}{2}\ln 2,\qquad \int_{0}^{\pi/4}\ln\sin\phi\,d\phi-\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\ln\cos\phi\,d\phi=-G$$
give
$$\int_{0}^{\pi/4}\ln\cos\phi\,d\phi=-\frac{\pi}{4}\ln 2+\frac{G}{2}.$$

Therefore
$$J=\frac{\pi}{2}\ln 2+4\!\left(-\frac{\pi}{4}\ln 2+\frac{G}{2}\right)=-\frac{\pi}{2}\ln 2+2G,$$
and the second part contributes $2J=-\pi\ln 2+4G$.

**Combining.**
$$I=\pi\ln 2+\bigl(-\pi\ln 2+4G\bigr)=4G.$$

**Numerical check.** $G\approx 0.9159655941$, so $4G\approx 3.66386$, consistent with direct quadrature of the integrand (which is $\pi/2$ at $x=0$ and decays like $2e^{-|x|}$).

$$\boxed{\,I=4G\,}$$
where $G=\displaystyle\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}\frac{(-1)^{n}}{(2n+1)^{2}}\approx 0.9159655941$ is Catalan's constant.
